patch_description: The best prior program (score 3367) used GRASP construction plus adjacent-swap local search. The recommendation says insertion moves beat swaps, but they explore different neighborhoods. My plan: build schedules with GRASP (greedy randomized construction picking among top-k cheapest next transactions using true incremental makespan), then improve each with a hybrid local search that alternates full insertion sweeps (move a transaction to any other position) with adjacent-swap sweeps, both evaluated on true makespan. Keep multiple restarts and return the best overall. Insertion moves can fix ordering mistakes that adjacent swaps cannot (e.g., moving a heavily-conflicting transaction earlier/later by many positions), while swaps unlock exchanges insertion can't reach cheaply. Evaluating on the true objective (get_opt_seq_cost) avoids heuristic misguidance.
